sections.h2: What should a Wilkinson County owner know about property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Two separate offices run the system, and a seller deals with both. The Board of Tax Assessors sets the value of your property, and the county tax commissioner sends the bill and collects the money. The Georgia Department of Revenue states the rule that matters most at a sale: whoever owned the property on January 1 is liable for that year's tax, and Georgia law gives no refund for the part of the year after you sell.

Wilkinson County covers about 452 square miles of central Georgia. Irwinton is the county seat and Gordon is the largest city. The Census Bureau counted 8,877 residents in 2020 and estimates 8,650 for July 2025. Houses here tend to stay with one household for a long time, since 92.3% of residents lived at the same address a year earlier.

Before you list or accept an offer, pull together these items:

  • your most recent tax bill and the assessment notice that came with the digest
  • proof of whether a homestead exemption is on the parcel
  • any mobile home location permit, if a manufactured home sits on the land
  • any lien notice or past-due letter from the tax commissioner

sections.h2: Which Wilkinson County offices handle which part of the tax process?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner collects, the assessors value, and a separate board hears disputes. Keeping the three straight saves a wasted trip to the courthouse in Irwinton.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills and collects property tax and handles vehicle tags. The office is at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136, Irwinton, GA 31042, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. The phone number is (478) 946-2232 and the mailing address is P.O. Box 182. Online payment carries a convenience fee.
  • Board of Tax Assessors and Chief Appraiser: appraises real and personal property, keeps tax maps and ownership records, receives returns and exemption applications, and certifies the digest. Call (478) 946-2076 or write to P.O. Box 189, Irwinton, GA 31042. The board meets on the first Wednesday of each month at 9:30 a.m. in the courthouse.
  • Board of Equalization: hears appeals of value, uniformity, taxability and denied exemptions. The county grand jury appoints its members, and the Clerk of Superior Court gives it clerical support.
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: each sets its own millage rate to fund the county budget and the schools.

The county also publishes a property record search and its tax digest with a five-year levy history on the county website, wilkinsoncounty.net.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply in Wilkinson County?
sections.html:
The rate depends on where the parcel sits, because each city adds its own levy on top of the county, state and school amounts. The Board of Assessors lists the 2025 totals below.

Wilkinson County 2025 total millage by jurisdiction, as listed by the Board of Assessors

Unincorporated county32.082

Irwinton37.892

One mill equals $1.00 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of fair market value. Mills apply after exemptions come off the assessed figure.

The county government's own levy is only one slice of those totals. For 2024 the Board of Commissioners published a notice that it would lower its county rate from 14.344 to 13.786 mills, which was still above the rollback rate of 13.227. A levy above rollback triggers three public hearings under Georgia law, and the notice scheduled them at the courthouse in January 2025.

sections.h2: When are Wilkinson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's site says county taxes are generally due by December 20. The date printed on your bill is the one to follow, because Georgia lets a county move the deadline to December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments.

State law gives each owner 60 days from the postmark of the bill to pay before interest begins. Penalties can be added to balances left unpaid after that. Ask the tax commissioner for the current interest and penalty figures when you request a payoff.

A few timing rules help a seller plan:

  • Tax returns for real and personal property are filed with the assessors between January 1 and April 1.
  • Once an initial real property return is on file, it renews automatically at the prior year's value. A new return is needed after you add improvements or acquire more land.
  • If taxes stay unpaid, the property can be levied upon and eventually sold. Confirm the status of any delinquent parcel directly with the tax commissioner.
  • A refund claim for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Wilkinson County property assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The appeal can challenge value, uniformity, taxability, or the denial of an exemption.

The state appeal form asks you to pick one of three paths: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. The Department of Revenue cannot override the local boards on an individual appraisal, so the decision stays at the county level unless you carry it to Superior Court.

Another route runs through the annual return. A taxpayer who files a new return during the January 1 to April 1 window and declares a different value starts the appeal process if the assessors do not accept it. Collect sales of similar houses nearby, photos of defects, and repair estimates before you file. Documented condition problems make the strongest evidence.

Filing an appeal does not erase the bill. Ask the tax commissioner whether to pay the undisputed amount while the case is pending, since any refund after a final value is processed automatically.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work for Wilkinson County owners?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption lowers the assessed value of the home you own and live in as your primary residence. Georgia sets a standard $2,000 reduction, and counties may add larger local exemptions. The Wilkinson County assessors page says the Chief Appraiser receives applications for the county homestead exemption.

You can apply at any point after the house becomes your residence, but the application must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year. Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption. A buyer who takes over the house will need to file their own application, because the exemption follows the occupant's residence.

If you are selling a house that you once lived in but now rent out, expect the exemption to fall away. Ask the assessors what the parcel's status shows today so the figures on your closing statement match.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when a Wilkinson County house sells?
sections.html:
Past-due tax is paid from the seller's proceeds at closing, and the title company asks the tax commissioner for an exact payoff. If the office has already recorded a lien, called a FiFa, it sits on the general execution docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court. Payment of the tax, fees and interest is what clears it.

The same January 1 rule applies to the current year. Because the full-year bill is the owner's responsibility, many contracts split the bill between buyer and seller by date. Put the split in the sales contract, because the county sends the bill to whoever it shows as owner.

Mobile homes follow their own steps. State guidance says an owner who places a mobile home in the county must obtain a location permit from the tax commissioner within 30 days, renew it each year between January 1 and April 1, and return the home for taxation by April 1. The assessors keep records for mobile homes that do not carry a homestead. Check that the permit and return are current before the sale.

sections.h2: What local housing facts affect a sale in Wilkinson County?
sections.html:
The market is small and rural. The Census Bureau puts the 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes at $86,300, with 80.5% of homes owner-occupied and 3,473 households. Median household income was $45,465 and the poverty rate was 20.6%. Builders pulled 18 permits in 2025, so new construction rarely competes with resale houses.

The 2020 census recorded 4,288 housing units, of which 16.3% were vacant. Wilkinson County School District is the only public district. Residents commute an average of 26.9 minutes to work.

If the parcel carries back taxes, confirm the payoff with the tax commissioner first, then compare offers with that number in hand.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: The county tax commissioner collects it. The office is at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136 in Irwinton and can be reached at (478) 946-2232. Questions about value go to the Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 946-2076 instead.

faqs.q: Are Wilkinson County property taxes due December 20?
faqs.a: Generally yes, according to the tax commissioner's website. Georgia lets a county choose an earlier date or installments, so follow the due date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Wilkinson County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice. File the written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and say which path you choose: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

faqs.q: If I sell in the middle of the year, do I still owe the whole year's tax?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 is liable for the whole year, and Georgia does not refund a partial year. Most sellers and buyers divide the bill by date in the sales contract.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for the homestead exemption in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: Apply through the assessors' office, where the Chief Appraiser receives homestead applications. Applications must arrive by April 1 to apply to that year's bill.
